back: Context compaction *evicts* the rule text — the model does not 'forget,' the instruction is physically removed. A control at 0/20 and restoration on re-pin prove it.
floor (rule visible) 0/20 → truncate (compaction evicts) 20/20 → pinned (re-inject after each compaction) 0/40.

front: Why is pinned 0/40 a fix, not just 'low'?
back: You test *equivalence*: the (pinned minus floor) upper bound sits under a pre-set +10% margin. Pinned 0/40 has a Wilson UB of ~8.8% → 'RESTORED,' indistinguishable from never losing the rule.
recency-truncate (evicts — the failure), head-tail (protective by construction, freezes the head), LLM-summarize (leaks ~5% per compaction — reported as a null / tail risk).

front: Why claim the gap's structure, not the point estimate?
back: The direct-request framing inflates the truncate rate above the paper's pooled ~38%. Honest move: claim the structure (present→compliant, evicted→violated, re-pinned→restored) and the interval, not '100%.'
It is protective by construction — it freezes the head of the context where the rule sits, so that specific rule is not evicted. Not a general guarantee for rules elsewhere.
